Temporary simulator copies Xcode makes to run tests in parallel and sometimes leaves behind. Safe to delete when no tests are running.
Earlier versions of Claude Code or Cursor Agent that stayed behind after updates. The version you run and the newest one are kept. Safe to delete.
Tool environments that pre-commit sets up to run your git hooks. Safe to delete; they are set up again on your next commit, which makes that commit slow.
App builds, templates and SDK data the Expo tools downloaded. Your Expo login is left alone. Safe to delete; Expo downloads what it needs again.
Source downloads pyenv and rbenv keep after installing a Python or Ruby version. Installed versions are left alone. Safe to delete.
Completion and update-check files that Oh My Zsh keeps. Safe to delete; they are recreated when you open a new terminal window.
Package downloads opam keeps for OCaml. Installed packages are left alone. Safe to delete; opam downloads them again when needed.
Browsers Puppeteer downloaded for automated tests. Scripts fail until it is installed again with npm install or npx puppeteer browsers install.
Packages conda unpacked to build your environments, which link to these files and keep working. Deleting frees less than shown; conda clean --all is safer.
Rendered frames EffectCraft keeps so effects preview without rendering again. Safe to delete; EffectCraft renders them again when you open a project.
Analysis results the Dart and Flutter language server keeps in ~/.dartServer so projects open faster. Safe to delete; the analyzer rebuilds them.
Hermes agent downloads and scratch space in ~/.hermes/cache. Clean it while Hermes is idle, since a running task may use it. Settings, keys and sessions stay.
Page and script caches of the browser Antigravity uses for web tasks, filled again as it loads pages. Sign-ins, history and extensions are left alone.
